name: North Korean FAKER Act proposed coordination framework

attribution.legal_posture: Congressional-office announcement and attached proposed/introduced legislation. The material remains a draft: the reviewed text displays an unassigned H.R. placeholder, while bill number, committee action, chamber passage, enactment, imposed sanction, and implemented-program status are unrecorded.

caveats: Introduced or proposed legislation remains a proposal; enacted sanctions and wrongdoing findings require later legal action.
This package covers source-level findings; named worker, applicant, facilitator, victim, entity and operational selector records require separate evidence.
The attached draft displays ‘H. R. __’; a bill number or later procedural status requires a separate official source.
The press release and bill draft form one congressional publication family; corroboration remains within that family.

statements: Coordinate allied sanctions and other restrictive measures against persons knowingly conducting or facilitating DPRK remote-worker schemes.
Increase allied information sharing about remote-worker schemes, money laundering, and proliferation networks.
Engage jurisdictions described as hosting, enabling, or failing to prevent the activity and support coordinated counter-evasion strategies.
Engage relevant private-sector experts and address artificial intelligence, synthetic identities, and other emerging technologies.
Authorize enhanced Rewards for Justice outreach and public attribution as appropriate.
Require an initial report after enactment and annual reports for two years.

sources.support: The congressional office says Representative Young Kim introduced the North Korean FAKER Act and describes proposed allied sanctions coordination, information sharing, counter-evasion assistance, Rewards for Justice activity, and annual reporting
sources.locator: Opening; paragraph beginning ‘Specifically’; five-item proposed-measures list

sources.support: The attached draft would authorize State Department coordination with allies and partners on restrictive measures, information sharing, engagement with enabling jurisdictions and private-sector experts, artificial intelligence and synthetic-identity risks, Rewards for Justice, public attribution, and recurring congressional reporting
sources.locator: Draft pp. 1-6; internal drafting timestamp July 21, 2026; especially sections 1, 3, and 4
